stem: Nandini buys a lamp marked $\mathrm{Rs}\,1200$. The shop adds $18\%$ GST on that marked price.

parts.text: Which claim correctly applies the tax?

options.text: The tax amount can be found with no reference to the marked price $\mathrm{Rs}\,1200$.
The same $18\%$ tax step also settles a later profit percent after the tax.
Selling price is $\mathrm{Rs}\,18$ because $18$ is the printed percent in the offer.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: GST is added as $18\%$ of the marked price being taxed, so multiply $1200$ by $1.18$ (or add $0.18\times 1200=216$) to get $\mathrm{Rs}\,1416$.

teacher.key_rationale: Tax uses the multiplier $1.18$ on the marked price $1200$, giving $1416$. Skipping the base, stretching the rule to profit percent, or reading the printed $18$ alone miss that hinge.
